about.title: Secured Loan Calculator - Collateral-Based Borrowing Cost & Payment Estimator
about.description: The Secured Loan Calculator helps you estimate monthly payments, total interest, and overall borrowing costs for loans backed by collateral (such as vehicles, savings, or property). Analyze interest rate scenarios, loan-to-value (LTV) ratios, and repayment terms to understand how collateral and fees impact affordability and risk.

howTo.title: How to Use the Secured Loan Calculator

steps.title: Enter Loan Amount
steps.description: Input the principal you plan to borrow based on the collateral value and required funding.

steps.title: Select Interest Rate & Term
steps.description: Choose the annual percentage rate (APR) and repayment term (months or years).

steps.title: Add Fees & Collateral Details
steps.description: Include origination fees, appraisal fees, and select the collateral type to reflect lender pricing.

steps.title: Review Monthly Payment
steps.description: See amortized payments and interest breakdown for each period.

steps.title: Compare Scenarios
steps.description: Adjust APR, term, or down payment to compare total cost and payoff speed.

tips: Lower LTV and stronger collateral often qualify for better rates.
Longer terms reduce monthly payments but increase total interest.
Check for prepayment penalties before making extra payments.

features.title: LTV & Collateral Impact
features.description: Understand how collateral value and LTV thresholds affect interest rates and approval odds.

features.title: Amortization Schedule
features.description: View principal vs. interest over time to see payoff progress and total interest paid.

features.title: Fee-Inclusive APR
features.description: Model origination and documentation fees to estimate true borrowing cost.

features.title: Scenario Comparison
features.description: Compare term lengths, APRs, and down payments to find a comfortable payment.

features.title: Prepayment Analysis
features.description: Estimate interest savings when making extra or lump-sum payments.

faq.a: A secured loan is backed by collateral (e.g., car, savings, or property). If you default, the lender may claim the collateral to recover losses.

faq.q: How does collateral affect my rate?
faq.a: Stronger, liquid collateral and lower LTV can reduce lender risk and generally qualify you for lower interest rates.

faq.q: Is it better to choose a shorter term?
faq.a: Shorter terms raise monthly payments but reduce total interest. Choose a term that balances affordability with cost savings.
Many lenders allow prepayment without penalty, but some charge fees. Check your loan agreement before making extra payments.
